item.research_question: How does the high entropy alloy 23Fe-21Cr-18Ni-20Ti-18Mn behave as an electrochemical sensor for ascorbic acid detection?
item.processing_route: Planetary ball milling for 15 h with a mill speed of 300 rpm and a ball-to-powder ratio of 6:1
item.test_conditions: Cyclic voltammetry in a phosphate buffer solution (PBS) of pH 7.2 with scan rates from 100 to 600 mV/s
key_findings: The crystallite size of the alloy decreases from 81 nm to 7 nm after 15 h of milling
The lattice parameter increases from 3.519 to 3.544 Å with a milling time from 0 to 15 h
The fabricated HEA-MCPE shows a strong electrocatalytic activity towards the oxidation of ascorbic acid
The 8 mg concentrated HEA-MCPE has a maximum current response compared to other concentrations
The electrode reactions during the electrochemical oxidation of ascorbic acid are diffusion controlled
The correlation coefficient for the plot of Ipa vs. scan rate is 0.9982, indicating a diffusion-controlled process
The calculated active surface area for the electron transfer process of ascorbic acid for HEA-MCPE is 0.0027 cm2
item.mechanism: The high entropy alloy forms a solid solution with refined crystallite size and increased lattice strain, leading to enhanced electrocatalytic activity
quotes: The fabricated HEA-MCPE showed excellent current sensitivity, stability, anti-fouling, and selectivity
The electrode reactions during the electrochemical oxidation of AA are diffusion controlled

records.text: Paper card. Question: How does the high entropy alloy 23Fe-21Cr-18Ni-20Ti-18Mn behave as an electrochemical sensor for ascorbic acid detection?. System: 23Fe-21Cr-18Ni-20Ti-18Mn high entropy alloy. Processing: Planetary ball milling for 15 h with a mill speed of 300 rpm and a ball-to-powder ratio of 6:1. Test conditions: Cyclic voltammetry in a phosphate buffer solution (PBS) of pH 7.2 with scan rates from 100 to 600 mV/s. Findings: The crystallite size of the alloy decreases from 81 nm to 7 nm after 15 h of milling; The lattice parameter increases from 3.519 to 3.544 Å with a milling time from 0 to 15 h; The fabricated HEA-MCPE shows a strong electrocatalytic activity towards the oxidation of ascorbic acid; The 8 mg concentrated HEA-MCPE has a maximum current response compared to other concentrations; The electrode reactions during the electrochemical oxidation of ascorbic acid are diffusion controlled; The correlation coefficient for the plot of Ipa vs. scan rate is 0.9982, indicating a diffusion-controlled process; The calculated active surface area for the electron transfer process of ascorbic acid for HEA-MCPE is 0.0027 cm2. Mechanism: The high entropy alloy forms a solid solution with refined crystallite size and increased lattice strain, leading to enhanced electrocatalytic activity. Quote: "The fabricated HEA-MCPE showed excellent current sensitivity, stability, anti-fouling, and selectivity"
